name: Underwater Enhancement and Detection Benchmark
description: Underwater image enhancement is such an important vision task due to its significance in marine engineering and aquatic robot. It is usually work as a pre-processing step to improve the performance of high level vision tasks such as underwater object detection. Even though many previous works show the underwater image enhancement algorithms can boost the detection accuracy of the detectors, no work specially focus on investigating the relationship between these two tasks. This is mainly because existing underwater datasets lack either bounding box annotations or high quality reference images, based on which detection accuracy or image quality assessment metrics are calculated. To investigate how the underwater image enhancement methods influence the following underwater object detection tasks, in this paper, we provide a large-scale underwater object detection dataset with both bounding box annotations and high quality reference images, namely OUC dataset. The OUC dataset provides a platform for researchers to comprehensive study the influence of underwater image enhancement algorithms on the underwater object detection task.
evaluation_method: mean Average Precision (mAP) for detection; PSNR/SSIM for image enhancement/quality assessment
general_score_metric: mAP (for detection) — PSNR/SSIM reported for enhancement
reputation: Used within the underwater imaging and robotics research communities to study how enhancement affects subsequent detection; recognized but domain-specific.
notes: Domain-specific (underwater) dataset coupling high-quality reference images with bounding boxes. Non-LLM benchmark; performance is sensitive to environmental conditions, imaging hardware, and annotation variability. May have limited scale relative to mainstream detection benchmarks.
